content.text: I’ve got the actual root causes now. One is a selection bug: personal (`me`) memories with an empty `scope_value` do not match once a GitHub username is available, so the “Claude Codex review spec” memory stayed active but never counted as injected. The other is accounting noise: we log internal prompts like `<task>...` as injection events, which pollutes the injection tab with follow-on task sessions instead of the originating user prompt.

I’m at the TDD stage now. I’m adding focused tests for both regressions before touching code: one for `me`-scoped manual memories created without a stored owner id, and one for lifecycle turn-start skipping system-generated task prompts so they don’t pollute injection history or counters.

I’m writing the red tests now against the two concrete failure modes I found in your saved state: implicit personal-scope memories not matching, and task-style prompts being counted as user injections. After that I’ll make the smallest possible fix in selection/lifecycle rather than reworking the TUI.

content.text: I’ve finished the affected package verification cleanly. I’m doing the final pass now: checking the exact diff and loading the completion-verification skill so I only report outcomes backed by the test results I just ran.

Fixed the two upstream issues causing the TUI to look wrong.

In [memoryloop.go](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/cmd/entire/cli/memoryloop/memoryloop.go), personal `me` memories with an empty stored owner id now still match for the current user when they were created manually. That addresses the case where a memory like “Claude Codex review spec” stayed active but never accumulated injection counts.

In [lifecycle.go](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go), memory-loop injection now normalizes prompts before matching/logging and ignores internal task-style prompts like `<task>...` and `<task-notification>...`. That stops the injection tab from recording follow-on task sessions as if they were user prompts.

I added regression coverage in [memoryloop_test.go](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/cmd/entire/cli/memoryloop/memoryloop_test.go) and [lifecycle_test.go](/Users/alisha/.superset/worktrees/cli/agent-improvements/cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle_test.go).

Verified with:
```bash
go test ./cmd/entire/cli/memoryloop
go test ./cmd/entire/cli
```

One important note: this fixes future matching/logging behavior. It does not rewrite already-saved bad historical rows in `.entire/memory-loop.json`.
